issue_context.title: make template selection test-able
issue_context.body:
We don't currently have the ability to test template selection during issue/pr creation and we
should.
comments: Also, we need tests for interactive mode in issue/pr creation

Can I take up the tests for the interactive mode?  
I tried it out locally, and the tests I wrote are working.

I can later on try stubbing the template file selection also

Got the solution!  
I feel we actually don't need to *exactly* stub the template file selection.
(Your comments here: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/4d11732a474fb4651704f9d9876d9f627e4283b5/command/issue.go#L362 and here: https://github.com/cli/cli/blob/4d11732a474fb4651704f9d9876d9f627e4283b5/command/pr_create.go#L218)
What I think is, instead of stubbing and putting demo files in the flow, we can actually utilize the existing template files in the flow.  
Let `gh` select our existing issue and pr templates from the file system, and then when the user selects that particular option of the template, we can directly check if the contents are proper.
(And we don't need to check for the change due to the user opening the text editor, as that is the job of the `surveyext` library, and we can assume that it is well tested.)
Also, we already have `github_template_test.go` for template content extraction stuff testing.

In case I was unable to put forth my ideas clearly, I believe that I will be able to show it better via a PR. (and commenting on my changes there)
sure, if you are up to it! Let me know if you have any questions or difficulties with the `AskStubber` and `CommandStubber` helpers.
oop, page was out of date. I'm happy to look at a PR and discuss there. Thanks for thinking about it and for checking in! Assign me as a reviewer, please.

review_comments:
My hope with template testing is that we're not reading from the filesystem. This can fail or change behavior as we change the repository itself.

I'd rather have a function wrapper around finding templates on the filesystem that can be overriden in tests to provide predictable results.

Oh. Okay. I was actually thinking that since the code is intended to read from the filesystem and we are also reading from the filesystem in the tests, it should not be a problem. Since changes to the file system would affect the code and the tests in the same way, so they would always be in sync
